title: Soft restart guardian and priority revocation hotfix
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Fix: introduce soft restart guardian to prevent restart cascades and add priority revocation backoff; improves SLO stability during node egress and regional failover.
description: Context: a production incident exposed a restart storm triggered by simultaneous tenant-priority revocations during regional egress which pushed nodes over the restart threshold and caused cascading SLO violations. This PR adds a small coordination layer (the "soft restart guardian") and soft-priority-revocation semantics to prevent mass restarts and to give SLO enforcer components time to reconcile. Motivation: reduce blast radius for aggressive revocations, stabilize SLOs during partial network/egress failures, and provide clearer telemetry for post-incident analysis. Key changes and rationale: 1) guardian controller: a lightweight leader-based coordinator that serializes node restart intent within a locality and implements exponential backoff with jitter before performing hard restarts; this prevents synchronized restarts. 2) revocation softening: priority revocations now carry a revocation-token TTL and a reclaim window; the enforcer applies a staged revocation (soft->hard) and honors a configurable grace window for KV cache draining. 3) safe-drain hooks: restarts and evictions now call a guarded drain API that attempts KV preservation and falls back cleanly after a timeout. 4) telemetry & alerting: new metrics restart_guardian.attempt, restart_guardian.delayed_count, slo.revocation.soft_count and a dashboard to track guardian decisions. 5) docs and operator guide: operational runbook and parameters added for rapid tuning during incidents. Commits: - implement guardian controller and tests - add revocation TTL + staged state machine - introduce guarded drain hook and abort paths - telemetry, dashboard and alert rules - operator docs and helm config entries Changed files (high level): pkg/serving/guardian.go, pkg/slo/revocation.go, cmd/agent/restart_controller.go, helm/charts/redwood/templates/guardian-config.yaml, observability/dashboards/restart-guardian.json, tests/e2e/restart-guardian.test.ts, docs/operational/restart-guardian.md Review conversation (summary): - Ravi Patel: requested stronger metrics around decision latency and a fast-path opt-out for emergency operations. Author response: added restart_guardian.decision_latency histogram and a config flag guardian.skip_soft_for_emergency. - Sofia Chen: asked for unit coverage of TTL decay edge cases; added table-driven unit tests and an e2e scenario simulating partial egress. - Liam O'Neill: suggested safer defaults for backoff jitter; author reduced default backoff multiplier and documented behavior. CI history: initial run flagged flaky e2e (tests/restart-guardian) related to timing; reran with increased test timeouts and CI passed. Risk/rollout: gated behind a helm feature flag enableRestartGuardian=false by default for customers on release channels; staged rollout to Dedicated clusters first for two weeks, then host-wide. Rollback plan: flip feature flag and revert config; restart_guardian is additive and defaults to non-intrusive behavior. Merge outcome: squash-and-merge after approvals from Ravi and Sofia; changelog entry included. Related work: ENG-2145 implements a follow-up that exposes per-tenant revocation telemetry and a CLI to force a soft-unwind during maintenance windows. Notes for on-call: if you see restart_guardian.delayed_count spikes with rising slo.revocation.soft_count, investigate egress throttles and KV sync latencies; use the operator docs to tune guardian.backoff.* and guardian.drain_timeout.
